notes: Unreal Engine Core exports a module calls through its import table, matched by library and mangled name. Windows x64 convention (args RCX, RDX, R8, R9; result RAX); register offsets as in crt_win64.json. Every entry is a declared assumption.

declares_assumptions.statement: FDebug::CheckVerifyFailedImpl and UE4Array_Private::OnInvalidArrayNum write no memory of the analysed module (no error delegate or log device calls back into it).
declares_assumptions.fails_when: A plugin that registers such delegates.

declares_assumptions.statement: The FName constructors change no memory the analysed module observes other than the FName they construct: the name pool, its locks, thread-local state and the blocks it allocates are Core-private, and no callback into the module runs (no allocator hook, ensure/log delegate or other reentrant diagnostic). The FName is 12 bytes (UE 5.1 editor build, case preserving).
declares_assumptions.fails_when: A module reading name-pool internals directly (FNamePool / name entry memory through an escaped pointer or export), hooking name creation, installing an allocator or diagnostic callback that writes module memory, or a Core build with a different FName layout (non-editor: 8 bytes).

declares_assumptions.statement: FMemory::Malloc never returns null on a normal return: out of memory is fatal in the supported UE 5.1 editor build (the allocator reports and terminates).
declares_assumptions.fails_when: A build or allocator (GMalloc replacement) that returns null on failure; a custom out-of-memory handler that resumes the caller.

entries.name: FMemory::Malloc
entries.notes: FMemory::Malloc(Count, Alignment): a new block's address (fresh); the allocator's own state is not this module's memory. Internal contract (library-internal-model-cuts): this is the complete observable effect also for callers inside Core; its private state is observed by no code using the model. Of Count (rcx) bytes; never null (ue-core-win64:fmemory-malloc-never-null): accesses inside the block are apart from the stack (docs 25.79).

entries.name: FName::FName(const WIDECHAR*, EFindName)
entries.notes: FName::FName(const WIDECHAR* Name, EFindName FindType): this = rcx. Writes exactly the FName at [rcx, rcx+12) -- ComparisonIndex, DisplayIndex, Number: UE 5.1 UnrealEditor builds are case preserving (WITH_CASE_PRESERVING_NAME), 12 bytes; checked against the UE testbed DLLs, whose code copies 12 bytes of the constructed FName -- with a value this model does not state (the name pool's index for the string at rdx; read with debt). Returns rcx. Reads the string at rdx and keeps no pointer it receives. Other memory this module can observe is unchanged: the name pool and its locks and allocations are Core-private state, and the constructor runs no callback into the module -- no allocator hook, ensure/log delegate (ue-core-win64:name-pool-private).
